SEC. 2. DEFINITIONS. In this Act: (1) Congressional intelligence committee.--The term ``congressional intelligence committees'' has the meaning given such term in section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3003). (2) Intelligence community.--The term ``intelligence community'' has the meaning given such term in section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3003). TITLE I--INTELLIGENCE ACTIVITIES SEC. 101. AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS. Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2027 for the conduct of the intelligence and intelligence-related activities of the Federal Government. SEC. 102. CLASSIFIED SCHEDULE OF AUTHORIZATIONS. (a) Specifications of Amounts.--The amounts authorized to be appropriated under section 101 for the conduct of the intelligence activities of the Federal Government are those specified in the classified Schedule of Authorizations prepared to accompany this Act. (b) Availability of Classified Schedule of Authorizations.-- (1) Availability.--The classified Schedule of Authorizations referred to in subsection (a) shall be made available to the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives, and to the President. (2) Distribution by the president.--Subject to paragraph (3), the President shall provide for suitable distribution of the classified Schedule of Authorizations referred to in subsection (a), or of appropriate portions of such Schedule, within the executive branch of the Federal Government. (3) Limits on disclosure.--The President shall not publicly disclose the classified Schedule of Authorizations or any portion of such Schedule except-- (A) as provided in section 601(a) of the Implementing Recommendations of the 9/11 Commission Act of 2007 (50 U.S.C. 3306(a)); (B) to the extent necessary to implement the budget; or (C) as otherwise required by law. SEC. 103. INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT ACCOUNT. (a) Authorization of Appropriations.--There is authorized to be appropriated for the Intelligence Community Management Account of the Director of National Intelligence for fiscal year 2027 the sum of $602,519,000. (b) Classified Authorization of Appropriations.--In addition to amounts authorized to be appropriated for the Intelligence Community Management Account by subsection (a), there are authorized to be appropriated for the Intelligence Community Management Account for fiscal year 2027 such additional amounts as are specified in the classified Schedule of Authorizations referred to in section 102(a). TITLE II--CENTRAL INTELLIGENCE AGENCY RETIREMENT AND DISABILITY SYSTEM SEC. 201. AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS. There is authorized to be appropriated for the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability Fund $514,000,000 for fiscal year 2027. TITLE III--INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY MATTERS Subtitle A--Intelligence Community Generally SEC. 301. RESTRICTION ON CONDUCT OF INTELLIGENCE ACTIVITIES. The authorization of appropriations by this Act shall not be deemed to constitute authority for the conduct of any intelligence activity which is not otherwise authorized by the Constitution or the laws of the United States. SEC. 302. INCREASE IN EMPLOYEE COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS AUTHORIZED BY LAW. Appropriations authorized by this Act for salary, pay, retirement, and other benefits for Federal employees may be increased by such additional or supplemental amounts as may be necessary for increases in such compensation or benefits authorized by law. SEC. 303. PROHIBITION ON INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY EMPLOYEES TRADING ON PREDICTION MARKETS. Section 102A of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3024) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection: ``(z) Prohibition on Use of Official Information or Position to Engage in or Manipulate Prediction Market Trading.-- ``(1) In general.--The Director of National Intelligence shall issue guidance prohibiting an officer or employee of an element of the intelligence community from, and shall ensure that any contractor to an element of the intelligence community is prohibited from, using nonpublic information to engage in trading on, or using their position to manipulate, a prediction market, except as may be necessary to conduct authorized intelligence activities. ``(2) Definitions.--In this subsection: ``(A) The term `nonpublic information' has the meaning given such term in the regulations (section 2635.703 of title 5, Code of Federal Regulations; relating to prohibition on the use of nonpublic information for private profit) and clarifying interpretive guidance issued by the Office of Government Ethics, as required by section 9(a)(1) of the STOCK Act (5 U.S.C. 13101 note prec.). ``(B) The term `prediction market' means a platform, company, or service that allows agreements, contracts, transactions, or swaps between users over the outcome of non-financial future events, such as sports, military actions, and elections.''. SEC. 304. ADDITIONAL POST-EMPLOYMENT RESTRICTIONS FOR PERSONS SERVING IN CERTAIN POSITIONS IN THE INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY. (a) Restrictions.--Title III of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3071 et seq.) is amended by inserting after section 304 the following new section: ``SEC. 305. ADDITIONAL POST-EMPLOYMENT RESTRICTIONS FOR PERSONS SERVING IN CERTAIN POSITIONS IN THE INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY. ``(a) Restriction.--A person who has served in a position in the intelligence community to which such person was appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, may not, during the 10-year period that begins on the date of the separation from service in such a position, knowingly act on behalf of a covered foreign entity as a lobbyist, agent, attorney, or other representative before any officer of employee of the United States Government. ``(b) Disclosure Requirement.--A person subject to the restriction in subsection (a) who accepts employment with, or is contracted for personal services by, a covered foreign entity shall notify the Director of National Intelligence in writing not later than 30 days after the date on which such person accepts such employment or enters into a contract for personal services with such entity. Such notice shall include-- ``(1) a description of the duties the person is expected to perform as an employee or under a contract for personal services; and ``(2) a certification that the employment or contract for personal services does not violate the prohibition under subsection (a). ``(c) Definitions.--In this section: ``(1) Covered foreign entity.--The term `covered foreign entity' means an entity owned, controlled, or directed by a foreign adversary (as defined in section 8(c) of the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2019 (47 U.S.C. 1607(c))). ``(2) Lobbyist.--The term `lobbyist' has the meaning given the term in section 3 of the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995 (2 U.S.C. 1602).''. (b) Applicability Date.--The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to any person who begins service in a position in the intelligence community (as defined in section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3003)) to which such person is appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, on or after the date of the enactment of this Act. Subtitle B--Matters Relating to Budget SEC. 311. INCLUSION OF COUNTERINTELLIGENCE OTHER THAN SECURITY FUNCTIONS AS A SPECIAL TOPIC IN BUDGET JUSTIFICATION MATERIALS. (a) Inclusion.--For the purposes of the congressional budget justification book for the National Intelligence Program (as defined in section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3003)) for each of fiscal years 2029 through 2031, and for any subsequent fiscal year as the Director of National Intelligence determines appropriate, information with respect to the aggregate amount of funding requested for counterintelligence other than security functions required to be included as part of the budget justification materials submitted to Congress under section 506(a)(4) of such Act (50 U.S.C. 3096(a)(4)) shall be included as a provision relating to a special topic in such congressional budget justification book. (b) Contents.--With respect to a fiscal year, the special topic provision included in the congressional budget justification book pursuant to subsection (a) regarding the aggregate amount of funding requested for counterintelligence other than security functions shall include-- (1) a summary of the primary activities and investments that such funding would support; (2) a disaggregation of such funding by program, budget category, intelligence discipline, and any other appropriate classification; (3) a comparison of such funding and the aggregate amount of funding made available for counterintelligence other than support for security functions during the preceding fiscal year; (4) the number of full-time equivalent civilian and military personnel assigned to the counterintelligence mission of the intelligence community other than in support of security functions; and (5) such other information as the Director of National Intelligence determines appropriate. SEC. 312. CONGRESSIONAL OVERSIGHT OF THE NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE PROGRAM BUDGET. (a) Findings.--Congress finds the following: (1) The Constitution vests Congress with the power of the purse, with provisions that refer to congressional authority to levy taxes, authorize the issuance of debt, and make appropriations to fund the Federal Government. (2) The executive branch's budget process exists primarily due to statutes enacted by Congress, which specify roles for the President, the Office of Management and Budget, and agencies. (3) By longstanding policy, Congress has authorized and funded classified intelligence programs without disclosing to the public the specific funding amounts or nature of such programs and activities to protect the national security of the United States. (4) Complex mechanisms within the executive branch have long been leveraged to enable the development, execution, and performance evaluation of classified budgets and to protect the classified programs of the intelligence community from discovery by foreign adversaries. (5) The classified nature of the intelligence community's budget requires a robust and efficient system of controls, to include classified reporting requirements, to ensure funding decisions are based on accurate information and that waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement can be detected as part of congressional oversight. (6) The National Security Act of 1947 prohibits the intelligence community from spending Federal funds on intelligence or intelligence-related activities unless specifically authorized by Congress and, when authorized, only according to the conditions provided by Congress. (7) Congressional authorization and appropriation decisions must be made based on the full cost and merit of programs and activities. (8) Documentation in support of the budget must be submitted to Congress in accordance with requirements specified in chapter 11 of title 31, United States Code, and other provisions of law. (9) The National Security Act of 1947 sets forth additional budget documentation requirements, including in sections 506G (50 U.S.C. 3103) and 506J (50 U.S.C. 3105a), related to the submission of classified budget materials to the congressional intelligence committees and appropriations committees (the ``committees''). (10) The amount of funding within the intelligence community's budget that is not documented in budget justification materials transmitted to the committees, and for which there is insufficient financial reporting during the fiscal year, is significant. (11) The committees are unable to make informed funding decisions based on the full cost and merit of proposed spending--to include outcomes, performance measures, prior investments, and cost benefits--when significant expenditures occur without prior budget justification and when financial reporting is not transmitted to the committees. (12) The lack of budget and financial reporting has impaired the ability of the committees to detect waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement within certain components of the intelligence community as part of independent congressional oversight. (13) Security considerations have been cited as justification for failing to produce budget documentation related to certain programs and activities. (14) Security decisions resulting in the withholding of budget documentation and financial reporting have been inconsistently applied among intelligence community programs and even within individual programs. (15) Current restrictions fail to account for the current transmittal, handling, and storage of classified information at the highest levels by the committees. (16) The opaqueness of portions of the intelligence budget reduces the committees' overall confidence in the soundness of financial management, a concern magnified by the failure of all but one element of the intelligence community to achieve an unqualified financial audit. (17) Full budget transparency to the congressional intelligence committees is not inconsistent with the need for continued secrecy of classified intelligence programs and activities and is fundamental to their success. (b) Congressional Oversight of the National Intelligence Program Budget.--The National Security Act of 1947 is amended by inserting after section 501A (50 U.S.C. 3091a) the following new section: ``SEC. 501B. CONGRESSIONAL OVERSIGHT OF THE NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE PROGRAM BUDGET. ``(a) Access to Full and Accurate Budget Documentation.-- ``(1) In general.--The Director of National Intelligence, the heads of departments containing agencies or organizations within the intelligence community, and the heads of all agencies or organizations within the intelligence community, in order to enable Congress and the committees specified in section 506J to carry out their constitutional responsibilities, shall ensure that the classified intelligence budget justification materials submitted under section 506J provide full, complete, and accurate budget documentation, including full, complete, and accurate cost, for each program, project, and activity of the National Intelligence Program. ``(2) Prohibition on withholding information and documentation.--Consistent with section 501 and other provisions of this title, information required by paragraph (1) to be included in such documentation shall not be withheld from such documentation, and documentation required by paragraph (1) to be submitted to the committees specified in section 506J shall not be withheld from such committees, on the basis of-- ``(A) the level of classification, compartmentation, or subcompartmentation of the program, project, or activity; or ``(B) any condition or restriction on access to information, except for conditions or restrictions under the procedures established by the House of Representatives and the Senate under section 501(d). ``(b) Segregation of Particularly Sensitive Sources and Methods Information.-- ``(1) In general.--Notwithstanding subsection (a)(2), the head of an element of the intelligence community, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, may segregate (such as within an annex) information about intelligence sources and methods that the head of such element considers to be of an exceptionally sensitive nature if the head of such element determines that-- ``(A) the segregation of such information is consistent with the need to protect such information; and ``(B) the information is not otherwise essential to the budget justification by the executive branch, or the budget evaluation by the committees specified in section 506J, of the full cost and merit of the programs, projects, and activities concerned. ``(2) Limitation on access.--The head of an element of the intelligence community may limit access to the information segregated under paragraph (1), but for each committee specified in section 506J the head of such element may not limit access to-- ``(A) the chairman and two appropriately cleared personnel designated by the chairman, for each committee; and ``(B) the ranking minority member and two appropriately cleared personnel designated by the ranking minority member. ``(c) Prohibition on Use of Funds.--None of the funds authorized or appropriated for programs and activities funded under the National Intelligence Program shall be available for obligation or expenditure by an element of the intelligence community to establish or enforce a restriction on access by the committees specified in section 506J to the information and documentation covered by this section, except as specifically authorized by this section.''. SEC. 313. BUDGET MATERIALS FOR OPEN-SOURCE INTELLIGENCE. SEC. 314. MODERNIZATION OF INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY BUSINESS SYSTEMS. (a) Findings.--Congress finds the following: (1) The lawful and efficient management of tax dollars by the intelligence community requires compliance with accounting principles and standards. (2) Elements of the intelligence community have been required since 2014 to produce annual, audited financial statements by section 509 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3108) and, prior to 2014, by the Accountability of Tax Dollars Act of 2002 (Public Law 107-289). (3) Unmodified or ``clean'' financial audits indicate that financial records are free from material misstatements and comply with Federal accounting standards. (4) As of 2026, only one element of the intelligence community has achieved an unqualified ``clean'' financial audit. (5) Failed audits have reduced congressional confidence in the soundness of the intelligence community's financial management, a problem compounded by the opaqueness of the classified budget and the failure of certain program elements to produce sufficient budget justification material. (6) In 2010, the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111-259) established policy supporting transformation and integration of the intelligence community's business systems to address inconsistent financial management and to improve the accuracy of financial reporting. (7) The Director of National Intelligence is required by law (section 506D of the National Security Act of 1947; 50 U.S.C. 3000) to develop and implement an enterprise architecture to cover all intelligence community business systems and the functions and activities supported by such business systems. (8) The Government Accountability Office (``GAO'') reported in 2018 (GAO-18-584SU) that the statutory requirement established in 2010 had not been satisfied. The GAO accompanied its report with ten specific recommendations, including that the Director of National Intelligence develop specific objectives and timelines to meet congressional intent. (9) The GAO continues to document a lack of progress in meeting requirements associated with the transformation and integration of intelligence community business functions and related systems, including the absence of a holistic plan. (10) The intelligence community has achieved extensive progress in the transformation and integration of information technology infrastructure, including the rapid growth and utilization by each of the elements of the intelligence community of tools and services hosted in secure cloud environments. (11) The development of a holistic plan to achieve business system transformation and to improve financial reporting must be a priority to enhance executive branch and congressional oversight of the intelligence community's expenditures, which are largely classified. (12) Therefore, all agencies and departments of the Federal Government with roles and responsibilities associated with the budget planning and execution of the intelligence community must modernize capabilities and processes, as appropriate, to improve financial reporting and ensure the secrecy of classified intelligence programs and activities and to support the implementation of the provisions of this section. SEC. 343. FRAMEWORK FOR COORDINATING AND CARRYING OUT OFFENSIVE COUNTERINTELLIGENCE OPERATIONS. (a) Requirement.--The Director of National Intelligence, the head of each department or agency of the United States Government that carries out offensive counterintelligence operations, and any head of an element of the intelligence community determined appropriate by the Director of National Intelligence, shall jointly issue a framework for coordinating and carrying out offensive counterintelligence operations. (b) Elements.--The framework under subsection (a) shall include the following: (1) Mechanisms for deconflicting and synchronizing offensive counterintelligence operations. (2) Principles to guide decision-making for maximizing the strategic impact of offensive counterintelligence operations, including with respect to weighing the value of disrupting law enforcement activities against the value of protecting operations intended to exploit, disrupt, or manipulate the target of such operations. (3) Mechanisms for resolving disputes among the elements of the intelligence community regarding offensive counterintelligence operations. (4) Common standards for the security classification and handling of offensive counterintelligence operations and information. (5) Common standards for training, tradecraft, and certifying individuals involved in offensive counterintelligence operations. (6) Any other matters the officials specified in subsection (a) jointly determine relevant. (c) Form.--The framework under subsection (a) may be issued in classified form. (d) Submission.--Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees the framework under subsection (a). (e) Implementation Briefing and Plan.-- (1) Briefing.--Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, each official specified in subsection (a) shall provide to the appropriate congressional committees a briefing on the progress made in establishing the framework under subsection (a), including a description of any obstacles to such establishment. (2) Plan.--Not later than 60 days after the date on which the framework is issued under subsection (a), each official specified in subsection (a) shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a plan to implement the framework. (f) Evaluation and Certification.--Not later than 180 days after the date on which the implementation plan is submitted under subsection (e), the Director of National Intelligence shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees an evaluation of the performance of the head of each department or agency of the United States Government that carries out offensive counterintelligence operations with respect to the requirements of the framework under subsection (a), including, with respect to each such head, either-- (1) a certification that the head is complying with such requirements; or (2) a written explanation for why the Director is unable to make such certification. (g) Definitions.--In this section: (1) The term ``appropriate congressional committees'' means the following: (A) The congressional intelligence committees. (B) The Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate. (2) The term ``foreign intelligence entity'' means a known or suspected foreign state or non-state organization or person that conducts intelligence activities to acquire information of the United States, blocks or impairs intelligence collection by the United States, influences the policy of the United States, or disrupts the systems and programs of the United States, including-- (A) the intelligence services and the security services of the government of a foreign country; and (B) international terrorists. (3) The term ``offensive counterintelligence operations'' means clandestine counterintelligence operations conducted against a target affiliated with a foreign intelligence entity for the purpose of penetrating, exploiting, disrupting, or manipulating the foreign intelligence entity to counter espionage, international terrorism, or other activities that threaten the security of the United States. SEC. 430. AIRBORNE INTELLIGENCE, SURVEILLANCE, AND RECONNAISSANCE STRATEGY. (a) Annual Strategy Required.--Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and on an annual basis thereafter, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Director of National Intelligence, the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, the Secretaries of the military departments, and the commanders of the combatant commands, shall submit to the congressional defense committees (as defined in section 101 of title 10, United States Code) and the congressional intelligence committees a strategy for Department of Defense airborne intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (in this section referred to as ``airborne ISR''). (b) Elements.--The strategy required by subsection (a) shall include each of the following: (1) A comprehensive assessment of the current airborne ISR enterprise of the Department of Defense, including-- (A) a summary of all airborne ISR platforms, systems, and payloads fielded or under development by each military department, including associated capability descriptions, inventory quantities, and operational availability rates; (B) an identification of the organizational entities responsible for programming, budgeting, and operating airborne ISR assets within each military department and within the joint force; and (C) an assessment of current contributions by each military department to joint and combined airborne ISR operations. (2) A prioritized articulation of validated requirements of the combatant commands for airborne ISR, including-- (A) a compilation of validated requirements for airborne ISR for each geographic and functional combatant command, disaggregated by mission area, priority, and theater; (B) an assessment of the degree to which current capacity and capability satisfies those validated requirements; and (C) a description of critical shortfalls in airborne ISR support, including gaps in platform availability, sensor coverage, data dissemination, and interoperability. (3) A Department-wide integration framework for airborne ISR, including-- (A) a description of the processes and mechanisms used to deconflict, task, and integrate airborne ISR assets across military departments in support of joint operations; (B) a description of current or planned initiatives to improve interoperability among airborne ISR platforms, ground exploitation systems, and dissemination networks across the military departments; and (C) an assessment of the sufficiency of existing joint doctrine, policy, and command relationships governing the employment and integration of airborne ISR assets. (4) Future investment priorities and programming guidance for airborne ISR, including-- (A) a description of the Department's planned investments in airborne ISR platforms, sensors, and enabling capabilities over the future-years defense program, with an explanation of how such investments address identified gaps and support combatant command requirements; (B) an identification of airborne ISR capabilities that are redundant or inefficient across the military departments, and a plan for optimizing such redundancies and inefficiencies; and (C) an assessment of whether current programming and budgeting processes sufficiently enable joint airborne ISR capacity planning, and any recommended reforms. (b) Elements.--Each briefing under subsection (a) shall include information relating to an implementation plan and framework for the establishment of the appropriate technical architectures and policy frameworks for the integration of intelligence described in subsection (a) in accordance with National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (relating to the integration, sharing, and use of national security threat actor information to protect Americans), issued on October 4, 2017. (c) Consultation.--The Director shall carry out subsection (a) in consultation with the heads of departments and agencies of the United States Government the Director determines appropriate. (d) Foreign Intelligence Threat Actors Defined.--In this section, the term ``foreign intelligence threat actors'' means individuals, organizations, or groups that are either-- (1) known or appropriately suspected to be engaged in espionage or other intelligence activities conducted against the national security interests of the United States by, for, or on behalf of foreign powers, organizations, or persons; or (2) known or appropriately suspected of seeking access to personnel, information, or assets of the United States Government for intelligence purposes. SEC. 515. REVIEW BY INSPECTOR GENERAL OF THE INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY OF POST-EMPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS. (a) Review.--Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community shall submit to the congressional intelligence committees a review of the compliance of each element of the intelligence community with post-employment requirements. (b) Elements.--The review under subsection (a) shall include the following with respect to each element of the intelligence community: (1) A description of the mechanisms of the element to provide training to employees and ensure compliance by former employees regarding post-employment requirements. (2) An evaluation of the degree to which former employees of the element are complying with post-employment requirements. (3) An evaluation of the timeliness of the element in-- (A) issuing regulations relating to post-employment requirements by January 22, 2023, pursuant to section 6301(d) of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (division F of Public Law 117-263; 50 U.S.C. 3073a note); and (B) implementing post-employment requirements. (4) Any other matter the Inspector General determines appropriate. (c) Definitions.--In this section: (1) The terms ``employee'' and ``former employee'' have the meaning given those terms in section 304 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3073a). (2) The term ``post-employment requirements'' means the requirements under section 304 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3073a) and Intelligence Community Directive 712. SEC. 516. EVALUATION OF CERTAIN COMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT AND SERVICES FOR RISKS TO THE UNITED STATES. (a) In General.--Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall-- (1) determine if any communications equipment or service described in subsection (b) poses an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons; and (2) submit to the congressional intelligence committees a report on the results of the determination. (b) Communications Equipment or Service Described.--A communications equipment or service described in this subsection is any communications equipment or service produced or provided by-- (1) Game Science Interactive Co., Ltd.; (2) Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd. (commonly known as ``DeepSeek''); (3) Hangzhou Yushu Technology Co., Ltd. (commonly known as ``Unitree Robotics''); (4) Hangzhou Yunshenchu Technology Co., Ltd. (commonly known as ``DEEP Robotics''); (5) BrainCo, Inc.; (6) Manycore Tech, Inc.; or (7) with respect to any entity described in any of paragraphs (1) through (6) (referred to in this paragraph as a ``named entity'')-- (A) any subsidiary, affiliate, or partner of the named entity; (B) any entity in a joint venture with the named entity; or (C) any entity to which the named entity has issued a license to produce or provide that communications equipment or service. SEC. 517. NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE ESTIMATE ON THREAT POSED BY ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF IRAN. (a) Requirement.--Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall submit to the congressional intelligence committees a National Intelligence Estimate on the threat posed by the Islamic Republic of Iran during the five-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act. (b) Elements.--The National Intelligence Estimate under subsection (a) shall include an assessment of each of the following: (1) The threat posed by Iran to the United States and the interests, partners, and allies of the United States. (2) The stability of the Iranian regime. (3) The status of the nuclear and advanced conventional weapons programs of Iran, including its ballistic missile and unmanned systems programs. (4) The status of, and threats to, the Strait of Hormuz. (5) The status of proxies of Iran in the Middle East region. (c) Form.--The National Intelligence Estimate under subsection (a) shall include an unclassified summary. (d) Certification.--Concurrent with the submission of the National Intelligence Estimate under subsection (a), the Director of National Intelligence shall, in consultation with the heads of other relevant elements of the intelligence community-- (1) certify to the congressional intelligence communities that such National Intelligence Estimate was prepared in accordance with all relevant analytical standards; (2) provide to the intelligence committees all intelligence reporting that was used to inform such National Intelligence Estimate, regardless of the classification level, control system, or compartment of the information; and (3) to the extent there exists any intelligence reporting that is relevant to such National Intelligence Estimate but was excluded from the production of such National Intelligence Estimate, provide to the intelligence committees-- (A) all such intelligence reporting, regardless of the classification level, control system, or compartment of the information; and (B) an explanation for why such intelligence reporting was excluded. findings.bill_quote: in paragraph (1)(A), by striking ``theft'' and inserting ``theft, including through distillation attacks,'';
findings.problem: Sec. 423(4) amendments to subsection (d), adding distillation attacks to theft and striking paragraph (2), and the subsection (a) change to "manipulate, deceive, or exploit", appear nowhere in the entry.
findings.fix: Add an item for Sec. 423(1) and (4): subsection (a) now covers efforts to "manipulate, deceive, or exploit"; subsection (d)(1)(A) now covers "theft, including through distillation attacks"; paragraph (2) of subsection (d) is struck.

findings.bill_quote: Evaluating artificial intelligence alignment, assurance, interpretability, safety, security, and transparency against risks, including backdoors, data poisoning, deception, hallucination, loss of control, shutdown refusal, sleeper agents, tampering, and other forms of unreliability.
findings.problem: The box omits the AI Security Center's new evaluation and testing-standards functions, the provisions that place the bill in scope, leaving 'among other duties' after a non-AI-safety determination.
findings.fix: Add: the Artificial Intelligence Security Center's functions now include developing best practices and standards for benchmarking, testing and evaluation of US and foreign AI models, and evaluating AI safety against risks including loss of control and shutdown refusal.

findings.bill_quote: There is a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Intelligence Community within the Office of the Director of National Intelligence who shall be appointed by the Director of National Intelligence.
findings.problem: The slot lists the government bodies bound but leaves out the new Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Intelligence Community, who carries four duties under §103N(c). The requires slot also omits this officer's duties.
findings.fix: Add "the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Intelligence Community" to Applies to, and add to Requires: the Officer must act as the DNI's chief representative for AI matters, assist in a long-term AI adoption strategy and with AI budget elements, and perform other AI duties prescribed by the DNI.

findings.bill_quote: (B) by striking ``within the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center of the National Security Agency'';
findings.problem: The entry does not mention Sec. 423(2)(B), which removes the AI Security Center's placement within the NSA Cybersecurity Collaboration Center. This is a structural change that the entry leaves out.
findings.fix: Add an item for Sec. 423(2)(B): subsection (b) of section 6504 is amended by striking "within the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center of the National Security Agency".

scope_check.reason: Sec. 423 makes the intelligence community's AI Security Center responsible for evaluating AI safety against loss of control and shutdown refusal, and for developing testing and evaluation standards for AI models. That is a binding intelligence-community AI safety and testing program (type 8a) aimed at advanced-AI risks (type 4), so the bill qualifies as a frontier-AI provision inside a broader authorization act.
